items.text: Giants cornerback Greg Newsome left Sunday's win over the Jaguars with an ankle injury and it will be some time before he will be back in the lineup.

items.title: Vikings "don't necessarily expect" Jordan Addison back this week
items.text: The Vikings didn't have wide receiver Jordan Addison in the lineup for Sunday night's game against the 49ers and his availability for Week 12 came up during head coach Kevin O'Connell's Monday press conference.

items.text: A report from NFL Media on Sunday morning indicated that the Colts have decided to pull the plug on hopes that wide receiver Alec Pierce will return to action this season, but it appears to have been premature.

items.title: Report: Giants DC Dennard Wilson had a virtual interview for Maryland head coaching job
items.text: Giants defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson has helped the team to a 6-3-1 record so far this season and he's landed on the interview list for a head coaching vacancy on the college level.

items.title: Panthers WR Jalen Coker is not in concussion protocol
items.text: Panthers wide receiver Jalen Coker was checked for a concussion in the fourth quarter of Sunday's game against the Ravens, but head coach Dave Canales had a positive update on his condition on Monday.

items.title: Quinnen Williams: We executed better on defense, but we still gave up 30 points

items.title: Dallas Goedert (shin) was listed as a limited participant on Monday’s estimated practice report.
items.text: Likely nothing to see here as the veteran tight end prepares for a divisional matchup against the Cowboys on Thanksgiving. Goedert’s 38-yard reception last week against the Steelers was his longer catch since Week 1, although the fact it was his only grab is troubling considering it was the first game with a healthy DeVonta Smith in a month. Goedert has been relegated to a top end TE2 against the Cowboys. - Mark Garcia

items.title: Saquon Barkley (neck/illness) was listed as a limited participant on Monday’s estimated practice report.
items.text: Barkley should be good to go for the team’s Thanksgiving showdown against the Cowboys Thursday despite the dual-tag designation. The veteran workhorse is coming off one of his best performances of the season against the Steelers, leading the team to their first win in two calendar months. - Mark Garcia

items.title: Jake Ferguson was listed as a “DNP” on the estimated practice report Monday.
items.text: Even though the team held a walkthrough ahead of their Thanksgiving matchup against the Eagles, the fact that Ferguson has yet to practice after injuring his ankle two weeks ago spells trouble for his potential availability in Week 12. Brevyn Spann-Ford and Luke Schoonmaker appear to be looking at another game atop the depth chart, with volume through the air most likely to concentrate further on CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. - Mark Garcia

items.title: Seahawks placed RB George Holani (knee) on injured reserve.
items.text: The move hurts far less than it would have earlier in the season when both Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price were unavailable. The change of pace option and special teams ace will now miss the next four games, at minimum, placing him in line to potentially return for Week 16 as the Seahawks make their final push toward the postseason. - Mark Garcia

items.title: Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) was listed as limited on Monday’s estimated injury report.
items.text: Kincaid missed Week 11’s game against the Dolphins with the same set of injuries despite being questionable entering the weekend. It’s quite possible the decision to sit him against the one-win Dolphins was more of a precautionary one ahead of the Bills’ Week 12 matchup against the Chiefs. We’ll see how the rest of his week unfolds, but Kincaid practicing in any capacity this week should be viewed as a good sign for his availability. - Zachary Krueger

items.title: Micah Parson has been cleared to return for the Packers’ Week 12 game against the Rams.
items.text: This one game a bit earlier than expected. While the hope was Parsons would return on Wednesday, the star pass rusher was listed as a limited participant in Monday’s practice, leaving some doubt as to whether or not he would be cleared for a return. Now, the Packers get back their 2025 sack leader who last played in Week 15 of last season, when he suffered a torn ACL on the road against the Broncos. items.title: Kenneth Walker (groin) was listed as DNP on Monday’s estimated injury report.
items.text: This wasn’t the news fantasy managers were looking for after going without Walker for each of the last two weeks. The Chiefs’ RB1 has been sidelined with a groin injury he suffered ahead of Week 10’s game against the Falcons, but there was early hope it would be a one-game absence. It was widely believed the decision to sit him against the woeful Cardinals was made to give him additional time to heal up before Week 12’s game against the Bills, but Monday’s DNP now draws his availability against Buffalo into question. items.title: Daniel Jones has cleared waivers and is now free to sign with any team.
items.text: Now that he has passed through waivers, Jones is officially a free agent and is free to sign with any team. While plenty of QB-needy teams could reach out for his services, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported early Monday that Jones will likely wait to sign with a new team and may leave the door open to signing with a contender later in the season that suddenly finds itself in need of a starting QB. - Zachary Krueger

items.title: Quinyon Mitchell (hamstring) did not practice on Monday.
items.text: It was an estimated session. Mitchell talked with reporters after leaving Sunday’s game with the hamstring ailment, implying it wasn’t a super serious injury. Still, on a short week, his status is up in the air. If he were ruled out, it would only help CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens on Thanksgiving. - Rivers McCown

items.title: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) is practicing in full ahead of Philadelphia’s Thursday game against the Cowboys.
items.text: We’re expecting the Eagles to force-feed Smith once more after his 57 percent target share on Sunday, leaving him as a plausible WR2 in an elevated matchup against the Cowboys defense. - Rivers McCown
